recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reintroducing requestedOn would reverse the later workflow-alignment decision; no follow-up is needed in FHIR core for FHIR-8198 unless Patient Care reopens the broader CommunicationRequest workflow naming decision.
issue_request: FHIR-8198 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request from the DSTU1/QICore ballot asking FHIR Core to rename CommunicationRequest.orderedOn to CommunicationRequest.requestedOn because the resource is a request and the change could not be made only in a profile.
initial_application: Git commit a452682b2ad0328e1dec9b63685546719904daf2 (#8044, #8198, #8466, #6251) changed the CommunicationRequest spreadsheet element from orderedOn to requestedOn and changed the matching search parameter from ordered to requested.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-10293 applied Patient Care workflow standardization to CommunicationRequest. Its implementation commit 999f9323adf4afe35f07a0276356db43f8786234 removed requestedOn from the resource model, added CommunicationRequest.authoredOn mapped to Request.authoredOn, updated examples and the search parameter to authored, and left source/fhir.ini conversion mapping from CommunicationRequest.requestedOn to CommunicationRequest.authoredOn. CommunicationRequest is an active resource in source/fhir.ini.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active CommunicationRequest definition no longer contains orderedOn, and authoredOn is the later workflow-aligned successor to the already-applied requestedOn change.

related_jiras.note: Published Patient Care workflow alignment replaced CommunicationRequest.requestedOn with authoredOn and updated examples/search parameters.
